proposed.text: A board item describes a door part that carries the door leaf and determines the axis about which the leaf swings. Which hardware family is being tested?

rationale.summary: A hinge or pivot supports the leaf and defines the swing axis.
rationale.explanation: Hinges and pivots are support-and-movement hardware. A strike receives a latch or bolt, a threshold treats the sill transition/seal, and a kick plate protects the lower face of the door.
rationale.takeaway: Ask first: does the part carry, secure, close, operate, protect, or seal the door?

proposed.explanation: A hinge or pivot supports the leaf and defines the swing axis.

proposed.text: Which set is best classified as finishing hardware rather than rough hardware?

options.text: Hinges, locksets, pulls, plates, and catches visible on the finished door
Nails, spikes, concealed rods, and construction screws buried in the work
Reinforcing bars, form ties, and embedded anchor bolts inside concrete
Temporary bracing, layout strings, and scaffold clamps used only during construction

rationale.summary: Finishing hardware is exposed and both functional and visible.
rationale.explanation: The article follows Salvan’s distinction: finishing hardware includes visible/touchable items such as hinges, locks, catches, pulls, and plates; rough hardware is normally hidden or constructional.
rationale.takeaway: If the occupant sees, touches, or operates it on the finished door, think finishing hardware.

proposed.explanation: Finishing hardware is exposed and both functional and visible.

proposed.text: A door detail shows two rectangular leaves mortised into the door edge and jamb, joined by interlocking knuckles around a pin. What hinge type is shown?

rationale.summary: A butt hinge is the standard two-leaf hinge with knuckles and a pin, commonly mortised at the door and frame edge.
rationale.explanation: The described anatomy—two plates/leaves, knuckles, and pin at the jamb edge—is the classic butt-hinge condition. A continuous hinge runs nearly the full door height, a concealed cup hinge hides in a cup/arm mechanism, and a parliament hinge projects the leaf farther away from the frame.
rationale.takeaway: Butt hinge = two leaves + knuckles + pin at the jamb edge.

proposed.explanation: A butt hinge is the standard two-leaf hinge with knuckles and a pin, commonly mortised at the door and frame edge.

proposed.text: A heavy, frequently used commercial door needs smoother movement and better wear resistance than a light residential bedroom door. Which hinge choice best fits the condition?

options.text: Loose-pin hinge selected only for removability

rationale.summary: Ball-bearing hinges reduce friction and suit heavier or higher-use swing doors.
rationale.explanation: The article distinguishes the ball-bearing hinge by its bearing collars/low-friction movement. Strap hinges may be decorative or used for gates/large leaves, but the described need is smoother high-use rotation. A loose-pin hinge emphasizes removability, not high-cycle wear resistance. A cabinet catch is not a support hinge.
rationale.takeaway: Heavy/frequent swing + smoother operation = ball-bearing hinge.

proposed.explanation: Ball-bearing hinges reduce friction and suit heavier or higher-use swing doors.

proposed.text: A maintenance plan requires a door leaf to be removable without unscrewing the hinge leaves from the frame and door. Which hinge feature directly answers that requirement?

options.text: Panic bar across the exit side

rationale.summary: A loose-pin hinge allows the pin to be removed so the leaf can be lifted away while the leaves remain fastened.
rationale.explanation: The requirement is removability of the door leaf, not egress release, sealing, or full-height load distribution. The hinge pin is the decisive feature.
rationale.takeaway: When the stem says removable leaf without unscrewing, look for loose pin.

proposed.explanation: A loose-pin hinge allows the pin to be removed so the leaf can be lifted away while the leaves remain fastened.

proposed.text: Which condition most clearly justifies a continuous hinge?

options.text: A tall or high-use door where support should be distributed along much of the door height
A small cabinet door where the hinge must be invisible when closed
A door that must swing clear of a deep reveal using extended hinge leaves
An exit door that must unlatch from pressure on a horizontal bar

rationale.summary: A continuous hinge, often called a piano hinge, extends along much of the door height to distribute support.
rationale.explanation: The article’s hinge comparison distinguishes continuous hinges by length and load distribution. Concealed cabinet-style hinges answer hidden appearance; parliament hinges answer wide throw; panic hardware answers egress release.
rationale.takeaway: Continuous hinge = long support line, not just another short hinge.

proposed.explanation: A continuous hinge, often called a piano hinge, extends along much of the door height to distribute support.

proposed.text: A large door is detailed to rotate from points at the floor and head rather than from knuckles fixed along the jamb edge. Which support type is most likely intended?

rationale.summary: Pivot hardware shifts the turning support to top and bottom pivot points instead of relying on jamb-edge knuckles.
rationale.explanation: The stem describes the axis and bearing points. Butt hinges are mounted along the jamb edge. Kick plates protect the lower face. A mortise lockset secures/latches the door.
rationale.takeaway: If the axis is at floor/head pivot points, answer pivot—not ordinary butt hinge.

proposed.explanation: Pivot hardware shifts the turning support to top and bottom pivot points instead of relying on jamb-edge knuckles.

proposed.text: An emergency-exit door must release when occupants push a horizontal bar across the interior face of the door. What hardware is described?

rationale.summary: Panic hardware releases an egress door by pressure on a horizontal bar.
rationale.explanation: A push plate may be pushed, but it does not necessarily release a latched exit door. A closer controls return to closed position. A threshold is a sill/sealing component.
rationale.takeaway: Horizontal pressure bar on an exit door = panic hardware.

proposed.explanation: Panic hardware releases an egress door by pressure on a horizontal bar.

proposed.text: A drawing note points to the manufactured assembly that includes the latch mechanism, trim, cylinder or operating parts, and faceplate. What is the best term?

rationale.summary: A lockset is the coordinated locking/latching assembly, not just the visible knob or lever.
rationale.explanation: The article warns against naming only the visible operating part when the complete assembly is meant. A kick plate protects the lower door, weatherstrip seals gaps, and a hinge leaf is one plate of a hinge.
rationale.takeaway: When the stem means the whole lock/latch assembly, answer lockset—not knob.

proposed.explanation: A lockset is the coordinated locking/latching assembly, not just the visible knob or lever.

proposed.text: An architect is selecting hardware for exterior doors of a coastal resort exposed to salt air. Which selection factor from the article should receive special attention?

options.text: Material/finish durability and resistance to weather or corrosive exposure
Only whether the hinge name is familiar from review notes
Only whether the hardware is the cheapest available item
Only whether the door has a decorative panel design

rationale.summary: Hardware selection must account for durability and exposure to weather or corrosive conditions.
rationale.explanation: The article adapts BCI’s selection factors to Philippine practice: function, mounting condition, material/finish, durability, and exposure matter. Salt air is a corrosion condition, so material and finish are not cosmetic afterthoughts.
rationale.takeaway: Exposure changes hardware selection; coastal conditions make material and finish a performance issue.

proposed.explanation: Hardware selection must account for durability and exposure to weather or corrosive conditions.
